extracted.intended_audience: literary critics, historians, and educated readers of biography and literary review
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative guidance for writing and judging historical prose, biography, and literary/political argument — identifying qualities that make historical narratives, prose, and poetry succeed or fail. Focuses on argumentation, style, narrative technique, and matching subject to authorial strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argumentative rigor / use of reason
rubrics_metrics.description: He does not seem to know what an argument is. He never uses arguments himself. He never troubles himself to answer the arguments of his opponents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A writer addressing political or philosophical subjects must give reasons, distinguish assertion from demonstration, answer objections, and supply a coherent chain of reasoning rather than relying on taste or rhetorical effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish assertion from demonstration; avoid logical fallacies
rubrics_metrics.description: It has never occurred to him, that a man ought to be able to give some better account of the way in which he has arrived at his opinions than merely that it is his will and pleasure to hold them. It has never occurred to him that there is a difference between assertion and demonstration ... that two contradictory propositions cannot be undeniable truths, that to beg the question is not the way to settle it, or that when an objection is raised, it ought to be met with something more convincing than 'scoundrel' and 'blockhead.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not found theories on single unexamined facts; avoid begging the question; when objections arise, answer them with reasoned counter-argument rather than abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic splendour and evocative imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: The utmost that can be expected from any system promulgated by him is that it may be splendid and affecting, that it may suggest sublime and pleasing images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For works of imagination and poetic systems, richness of image and emotional effect can be a primary merit — but such splendour cannot substitute for logical coherence when the subject demands it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain conventional probability in works of art
rubrics_metrics.description: It has something of invention, grandeur, and brilliancy. But, like them, it is grotesque and extravagant, and perpetually violates even that conventional probability which is essential to the effect of works of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even imaginative writing should preserve a conventional plausibility; grotesque extravagance that breaks the reader’s sense of probability undermines artistic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match genre and task to the author's strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: His success has almost always borne an inverse proportion to the degree in which his undertakings have required a logical head. His poems, taken in the mass, stand far higher than his prose works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should choose subjects and genres suited to their natural gifts (e.g., a poet may excel at imagery and narration but fail where sustained logical analysis is required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to factual outline in biography/history
rubrics_metrics.description: The Life of Nelson is, beyond all doubt, the most perfect and the most delightful of his works. ... The necessity of adhering to the real course of events saved Mr. Southey from those faults which deform the original plan of almost every one of his poems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biographical and historical subjects often benefit from sticking closely to the documented course of events; a clear factual outline can constrain and improve the writer’s imagination and prevent speculative excesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities required of a philosophic historian
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject which he has at last undertaken to treat, is one which demands all the highest intellectual and moral qualities of a philosophical statesman, an understanding at once comprehensive and acute, a heart at once upright and charitable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex historical and political subjects require comprehensive intellect, acute analysis, moral balance, and the ability to develop causes and consequences logically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control passions when undertaking intellectual tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: The adventure was manifestly one which could be achieved only by a profound thinker, and one in which even a profound thinker might have failed, unless his passions had been kept under strict control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must restrain personal passions and prejudices when treating delicate or profound topics, or risk distorting judgment and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative skill / art of narration
rubrics_metrics.description: There are charming specimens of the art of narration in both of them. The Life of Wesley will probably live. Defective as it is, it contains the only popular account of a most remarkable moral revolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear storytelling and well-crafted narrative passages are a key virtue in histories and biographies; episodes told 'prettily' or vividly can redeem other flaws and engage readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style: beauty and purity of English
rubrics_metrics.description: On such occasions his writings are rescued from utter contempt and derision solely by the beauty and purity of the English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elegant, pure, and engaging prose style can compensate to some extent for weaknesses in argument or judgement; stylistic command is a substantive evaluative criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humour should avoid quaint or flippant dullness
rubrics_metrics.description: He very often attempts to be humorous, and yet we do not remember a single occasion on which he has succeeded further than to be quaintly and flippantly dull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humour in prose must be genuinely entertaining and appropriate to tone; attempts at drollery that produce quaint or flippant dullness are faults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vivid contemporary examples and primary anecdotes
rubrics_metrics.description: The birthday of our ally was celebrated with as much enthusiasm as that of our own sovereign; and at night the streets of London were in a blaze with illuminations. Portraits of the Hero of Rosbach ... were in every house. One of Whitfield’s hearers ... made the following exquisitely ludicrous entry in a diary ... 'O! how good it is to pray and fight!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In historical narrative, deploying concrete contemporary examples, public reactions, and preserved anecdotes or diary entries helps convey public sentiment and gives colour and authority to claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie political/military events to cultural and literary consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest masters of German poetry and eloquence have admitted that ... he did much to emancipate the genius of his countrymen from the foreign yoke; and that, in the act of vanquishing Soubise, he was, unintentionally, rousing the spirit which soon began to question the literary precedence of Boileau and Voltaire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good historiography traces unintended cultural and literary consequences of political actions, showing broader impact beyond immediate military or diplomatic outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict socioeconomic/logistical consequences with concrete detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere contributions levied by the invaders amounted, it was said, to more than a hundred millions of dollars; ... The fields lay uncultivated. The very seed-corn had been devoured ... Near fifteen thousand houses had been burned to the ground. The population of the kingdom had in seven years decreased to the frightful extent of ten per cent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To convey the true cost and effect of events like war, include economic figures, demographic impacts, material destruction, and observable social consequences — these specifics strengthen historical argument and narrative weight.
